1.explanation:
• BpmnReplace.replaceElement and its helper shouldToggleCollapsed: When replacing a Call Activity with a Sub-Process, shouldToggleCollapsed returns true and triggers only a collapse toggle (modeling.toggleCollapse) with an early return. This skips the normal replace path that would copy the old width/height or apply the target’s dimensions, so the shape never resizes.  
• ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.expandedBounds and its postExecuted handler: After the toggleCollapse command, postExecuted always recomputes the expanded bounds based on default sizes and child bounds (which are empty), ignoring the original shape size. As a result, the expanded Sub-Process snaps to a default (small) size rather than growing to the prior dimensions. Together, these code paths cause the Sub-Process to remain at the Call-Activity size and lose the ability to switch back via the menu.
1.bug_scenario: After converting a Call Activity into an expanded Sub-Process via the wrench (replace) menu, the element visually remains at the small Call-Activity size (like a Task) instead of stretching to the Sub-Process default or retaining its prior dimensions. Moreover, the replace menu then only shows “Event Sub Process,” preventing the user from reverting back to a Call Activity.

2.explanation:
• BpmnReplace.replaceElement and shouldToggleCollapsed: These functions drive the core replace operation (task→call activity→subprocess). The code that copies or resets width+height on newElement only runs for certain BPMN:Activity replacements and contains a TODO about respecting min/max size. In our scenario (call activity→expanded subprocess), the sizing logic does not trigger, so the shape remains at its old dimensions.
• ToggleElementCollapseBehaviour.postExecuted (‘shape.toggleCollapse’): This handler recalculates and applies new bounds when collapsing/expanding via modeling.toggleCollapse, but it is never invoked in the replace operation. As a result, replacing directly to an expanded subprocess never goes through the resize logic.
• ReplaceMenuProvider.getEntries: This function builds the wrench menu entries. After the replace, it filters out the Call Activity option for a collapsed or expanded subprocess, only leaving Event Sub Process. Thus the user cannot revert back to a call activity once they’ve replaced it, leading to the dead end described in the bug report.
2.bug_scenario: The user starts with a task, turns it into a call activity (wrench→Call Activity), then immediately turns that call activity into an expanded subprocess (wrench→Sub-Process expanded). The resulting element stays at the call-activity size (so it visually looks like a task) instead of resizing to the default expanded-subprocess dimensions. Furthermore, the wrench menu no longer offers “Call Activity”—only “Event Sub Process”—so the user cannot revert, effectively reaching a dead end.
